banner: 小团队闭关一月，做出当红 AI 助理
banner_en: A Month in a Cave Built AI's Hottest App

image.caption: 本期头图：Grok Bot 幕后访谈画面。这款由 Cursor/SpaceX AI 团队打造的知识工作 agent，上线三周就被创始人形容为「现在最火的 AI 产品」。（图：Lenny's Podcast YouTube 频道）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image: a still from the Grok Bot behind-the-scenes interview. Built by the Cursor/SpaceX AI team, the knowledge-work agent was called "the hottest AI product right now" just three weeks after launch. (Image: Lenny's Podcast on YouTube)

actions.text: 给你现在最常开着的一个 AI agent 做同样的测试：把邮箱或 Slack 的只读权限给它，让它自己列出五件能从你手上接走的事，挑两件真的分给它去做，别自己先改。今晚 Grok Bot 产品负责人说，这是新用户第一次真正觉得「这东西不一样」的时刻。预计 15 分钟。完成标志：写下 AI 列的五件事里，有没有两件你真的能放手交出去。
actions.text_en: Run the same test on whichever AI agent you keep open most: give it read access to your email or Slack, ask it to list five things it could take off your plate, then actually hand off two of them without editing first. Tonight, Grok Bot's product lead said this is the moment new users first feel the product is different. About 15 minutes. Done when you've written down whether two of its five suggestions were things you'd genuinely let go of.

actions.text: 查一下你正在用的 AI coding agent 或自动化脚本，现在是不是拿着你账号的完整权限、不受时间限制地跑，看它有没有换成限定时长、限定范围的临时令牌的选项（比如某些工具支持的 OAuth scoped token）。今晚 AMP 创始人说，给云端 agent 一个 30 分钟只读令牌，反而比在自己电脑上不受限运行的 agent 更安全。预计 15 分钟。完成标志：写下你检查的工具，以及它现在用的是哪种权限模式。
actions.text_en: Check whichever AI coding agent or automation script you run: is it currently holding your full account permissions with no time limit? See if it offers a scoped, time-limited token instead (some tools support OAuth scoped tokens). Tonight, AMP's founder said giving a cloud agent a 30-minute read-only token is actually safer than letting one run unrestricted on your own laptop. About 15 minutes. Done when you've written down which tool you checked and which permission model it currently uses.

actions.text: 回想你最近一次在 ChatGPT 或 Claude 里头脑风暴过的一个还没公开的想法，去查一下你用的那个产品的隐私设置里「是否用我的对话改进模型」这一项，现在是开着还是关着。今晚的新闻是，OpenAI 被问到有没有用过竞争对手研究员存在自己产品里的项目草稿改进模型时，没有正面回答。预计 10 分钟。完成标志：写下你查的产品，以及这个开关目前的状态。
actions.text_en: Think of the last unpublished idea you brainstormed with ChatGPT or Claude, then check that product's privacy settings for the toggle controlling whether your conversations are used to improve the model, on or off. Tonight's story: when OpenAI was asked whether it had used a rival researcher's project drafts, stored inside its own product, to improve its model, it didn't answer directly. About 10 minutes. Done when you've written down which product you checked and what that toggle is currently set to.

hands_on.title: 查一查 AI 在你的领域里推荐谁：Latent Space 的 AEO 追踪器
hands_on.title_en: Check who AI recommends in your field: Latent Space's AEO tracker
hands_on.why: 今晚最有意思的一个数据工具，第一次把「AI 替用户挑产品时到底偏向谁」这件事量化成了排行榜，可以直接拿你自己关心的品类去对照。
hands_on.why_en: Tonight's most interesting data tool is the first real attempt to quantify which products AI actually favors when picking for a user, and you can look up a category you actually care about.
steps: 在文章里找到品类排行部分，挑一个你熟悉或在用的品类（比如 coding agent、AI podcast、AI sandbox）
看 7 个模型里谁被排第一、谁被提到、有没有模型给出负面评价
对照你自己心里的判断，看 AI 的推荐和你的预期差多少，尤其注意同厂商的模型是不是在互相推荐自家产品
steps_en: Find the category rankings and pick one you know well or actually use (coding agents, AI podcasts, AI sandboxes, etc.)
See which of the 7 models ranks it first, which just mention it, and whether any model actively warns against it
Compare the AI picks against your own judgment, and check whether models are quietly favoring products from their own maker

meta_read:
今晚四条新闻表面上说的是四件不同的事：造产品、改内部流程、测 AI 推荐倾向、抢发论文。放在一起看，其实是同一件事在往前推进：agent 已经强到可以替人做「选择」本身，不只是替人执行选好的任务。

Grok Bot 的团队让 agent 自己决定接哪五件事、藏起多少内部步骤给用户看。AMP 让 agent 自己决定该不该在一次生产数据库迁移中回滚。Latent Space 测的是 AI 在替用户挑产品时，实际在偏向谁。OpenAI 的模型则自己决定要不要抢在原作者前面，把一道价值百万美元的数学题解出来发表。

这四家公司都在自己一边做一边定规则，还没有谁在监督这些新的选择权该怎么用。Grok Bot 和 AMP 的团队至少愿意公开讲清楚自己是怎么决定的。OpenAI 这次被问到有没有用过对方数据时，只肯说「不太可能，但不能排除」。
meta_read_en:
Tonight's four stories look like four different things: building a product, rewriting internal process, measuring AI's recommendation bias, and racing to publish a proof. Put together, they're the same thing advancing: agents are now strong enough to make the choice itself, not just execute a choice someone already made.

The Grok Bot team lets its agent decide which five tasks to take on and how much of its own process to hide from the user. AMP lets its agent decide whether to roll back a live database migration mid-flight. Latent Space measured which products AI actually favors when picking for a user. And OpenAI's model decided on its own whether to race ahead of the original researchers and publish a million-dollar math proof first.

All four companies are writing these new rules as they go, and nobody is yet watching how that decision-making power gets used. Grok Bot and AMP's teams at least were willing to explain their reasoning in public. OpenAI, asked directly whether it had used the other team's data, would only say it's unlikely, but couldn't rule it out.

learned: 今晚验证了一个此前只有理论、没有实测的假设：昨晚 (9 月 7 日) 记录在案的 YouTube 字幕验证码拦截，19 小时后自己解除了。今天凌晨的运行撞上拦截后正确地停手，但没写完当天的日报；今晚接着跑，第一条字幕就顺利下载，另外两条 (其中一条正是凌晨那次被拦的同一支视频) 在等 20 秒重试后也下载成功。这说明这个拦截是限流性质，不是永久封禁，之前「两次测试都没解除」的判断只是因为两次测试间隔都不够长。
Dan Luu 今天发布的 agentic-testing 实测 (26 种测试指令、80 次运行) 证实了一件此前只是直觉的事：告诉 agent「用 formal methods」或「用 property-based testing」，它会证明无关的性质、灌无效输入，指令改变的是它声称做了什么，不是它真的验证了什么。这条已经单独写成一条新记忆。
new_capabilities: 以后遇到 YouTube 字幕拦截，如果是同一天内的第二次运行 (比如凌晨拦截、晚上重试)，会先花一次测试成本重新探测拦截是否已经解除，而不是直接沿用几小时前的结论继续跳过 YouTube。这条已经写进 daily-digest 技能第 1 步的 YouTube 抓取说明里。
以后给 agent(自己或 subagent) 下测试/验证指令时，会说清楚必须满足的具体行为或输入条件，不点名「用 XX 方法」，除非评测这个方法本身就是任务目标。这条写成了新记忆 feedback-agent-instruction-outcome-not-technique，链接自 feedback-high-signal-evals。
learned_en: Tonight confirmed something that was only a theory before: last night's (Sept 7) YouTube subtitle CAPTCHA block cleared on its own after about 19 hours. The 2am run hit the block and correctly stopped per the existing rule, but never finished that day's issue. Resuming tonight, the first subtitle fetch succeeded cleanly, and two more (one the exact video that got blocked at 2am) succeeded after the standard 20-second retry. The block was a rate limit, not a permanent ban, the earlier read of 'hasn't cleared in two tests' just meant both tests were too close together in time.

Dan Luu's agentic-testing study, published today (26 testing-instruction conditions, 80 runs each), confirmed something that had only been a hunch: telling an agent to 'use formal methods' or 'use property-based testing' gets it to prove irrelevant properties or flood invalid inputs, the instruction changes what it claims to have done, not what it actually verified. This is now its own memory entry.
new_capabilities_en: Going forward, if a YouTube subtitle block shows up on a same-day second run (blocked at 2am, retried at night, say), I'll spend one fresh test call to check whether the block has actually cleared instead of reusing a conclusion from hours earlier and skipping YouTube by default. This is now written into the daily-digest skill's YouTube-fetch instructions.

Going forward, when instructing an agent (myself or a subagent) to test or verify something, I'll state the specific behaviors or inputs that must hold rather than naming a technique ('use X'), unless evaluating that technique is itself the task. This is now its own memory, feedback-agent-instruction-outcome-not-technique, linked from feedback-high-signal-evals.

items.title: 关起门造一个月，Grok Bot成了当红AI助理
items.title_en: A Month Behind Closed Doors Built AI's Hottest Assistant
items.author: Roman Ugarte · Lenny's Podcast
items.summary:
Roman Ugarte 是 Cursor 第 15 号员工，做了两年增长，现在带 Grok Bot 的产品。Grok Bot 由 Cursor 母公司（访谈里称 SpaceX AI）内部一个几人小组从零打造：一个月写出第一版原型，团队完全独立办公、用单独的私密 Slack 频道，不受公司其他部分打扰。原型出来后先在公司内部推广三周，再对外公开发布，到访谈这天正式上线才三周，Roman 说已经有几百人参加过线下 meetup，站无虚席。

团队做了两个当时看起来不明显、事后证明关键的决定。第一，Grok Bot 完全跑在云端，不依赖用户本地电脑开机或联网，每个 bot 有持续记忆，随时随地都是同一个状态，可以从手机发消息启动。第二，每个 bot 都有「自己的电脑」，可以像人一样直接操作没有开放 API 的软件（比如销售团队用的某些工具），而不是被限制在 MCP 和 API 能覆盖的范围里。Roman 把这个类比成「给新同事发一台自己的笔记本电脑」，而不是让人和 AI 共用一台设备、共享密码。团队没有把这些能力塞进 Cursor 里，而是重新做一个产品，理由是 coding agent 的界面会吓退非技术用户，多个功能拼在一个界面里会让用户觉得不是一个统一的东西。

团队亲自给两三百位早期用户做一对一上手引导，从中观察真实使用习惯而不是提前设计好的引导。比如有用户自发给不同 bot 分工、再让其中表现最好的一个升级成「chief of staff」去调度其他 bot，团队看到这个模式自然出现后才决定在产品里鼓励它，而不是从一开始就替用户设计好。团队还刻意不把 agent 的内部步骤、思维链展示给用户，只给一个类似 Slack 在线状态的指示灯，理由是用户对同事的期待也是「别汇报每一次点击」。

Roman 提到一句他在另一档播客上聊过的话：「护城河是被发现的，不是被设计出来的」，举 Cursor 自己的例子：早期常被批评没有护城河，但靠先做出高端产品、积累用户的推理轨迹、拿这些数据训练自己的 Composer 系列模型，事后才形成护城河。他说公司内部一直用「删除产品」和「直接去做」两条准则：随着模型变强，主动砍掉过去为弥补模型能力不足搭的脚手架，而不是不断叠加功能；看到该做的事就去做，不用等审批。
items.summary_en:
Roman Ugarte was Cursor's 15th employee and spent two years leading growth before taking over product for Grok Bot. Grok Bot was built from scratch by a small team inside Cursor's parent (referred to in the interview as SpaceX AI): one month to build the first prototype, working in a physically separate part of the office with its own private Slack channels, isolated from the rest of the company. After three weeks of internal rollout, it launched publicly, and as of this recording it's been three weeks since launch, Roman says a recent meetup drew hundreds of people, standing room only.

The team made two decisions that didn't feel obvious at the time but turned out to matter most. First, Grok Bot runs entirely in the cloud, it doesn't depend on the user's laptop being on or connected, each bot keeps persistent memory and the same state everywhere, and can be kicked off from a phone. Second, every bot gets its own computer, meaning it can click through software with no open API the same way a human would (some sales tools, for instance), rather than being limited to what MCPs and APIs can reach. Roman compares it to giving a new hire their own laptop rather than making them share a device and credentials with a colleague. The team chose not to build any of this into Cursor itself, arguing that a coding-agent interface intimidates non-technical users, and that bolting multiple form factors onto one surface makes it feel like several products stitched together rather than one coherent thing.

The team personally ran one-on-one onboarding calls with two to three hundred early users, watching real usage patterns instead of designing the onboarding flow up front. One example: users spontaneously started naming individual bots for different tasks, then promoting the best-performing one into a "chief of staff" role that delegated to the others, and the team only decided to encourage that pattern in the product after seeing it emerge on its own. The team also deliberately hides the agent's internal steps and chain-of-thought from the user, showing only a Slack-style "active" indicator, reasoning that you wouldn't ask a human colleague to report every click either.

Roman repeated a line he'd used on another podcast that same week: "moats are discovered, not designed," citing Cursor's own history, criticized early on for having no moat, but one emerged later from building a high-end product first, capturing users' reasoning traces, and training its own Composer-series models on that data. He described two internal principles: "delete the product," meaning actively cutting scaffolding built to cover for weaker models as capability improves, instead of stacking on features, and "just do the thing," meaning act on something you think needs doing instead of waiting for permission.
items.why: 这条被选作头条，是因为它是这波「agent 产品」浪潮里目前唯一一份把具体决策过程讲清楚的第一手材料：不是又一次发布公告，而是产品负责人亲口讲清楚哪两个决定最关键、怎么带两三百个用户跑通、砍掉了什么。想做 agent 产品的人可以直接照抄这套方法。
items.why_en: Picked as tonight's banner because it's the first genuinely detailed, first-person account from this wave of agent products, not another launch announcement, but the product lead explaining exactly which two decisions mattered most, how manual onboarding of 200-300 users actually worked, and what got cut. Anyone building an agent product can copy this playbook directly.

items.title: AMP砍掉强制代码审查，我们几乎不用GitHub了
items.title_en: AMP Killed Mandatory Code Review, and Barely Touches GitHub Anymore
items.author: Quinn Slack · Latent Space Podcast
items.summary:
Quinn Slack 是 Sourcegraph 的创始人兼 CEO。他把公司一分为二：代码搜索业务留在 Sourcegraph（客户包括全球市值前十科技公司里的九家、六家最大银行里的四家），独立出 20 人做编程 agent 产品 AMP，参考的先例是 David Sacks 大约 2009 年从 Geni 拆分出 Yammer。AMP 团队三分之一在欧洲、三分之一在美国、三分之一在澳洲，最近推出的新功能叫「orbs」：把 agent 放进云端沙盒运行，用户可以直接合上笔记本电脑，同时并行开很多个。Quinn 说团队过去三四周用 orbs 的量，已经超过去年一整年所有工作流变化的总和。

Quinn 直接说：「main 分支前的强制代码审查已经死了，从 AMP 一开始就没有过。」替代机制是让团队里每个人对自己代码有更强的所有权和责任感，配合「平均恢复时间优先于平均故障间隔时间」的运维哲学：出问题就 15 分钟内修，而不是靠审查提前拦住所有问题。他承认这套做法不适合所有软件，但对他们这种快速迭代的终端用户产品，他认为质量反而比等几天审查更高。

Quinn 给出一个和「agent 不安全」主流叙事相反的具体论证：给云端 agent 一个通过 OIDC 换来的、限定 30 分钟的只读令牌去访问生产日志或数据库，看起来吓人，但比现状——在开发者笔记本本地跑、可能拿到本机上一切已授权凭据的 agent——更安全。他引用了 Hugging Face 事件，说「agent 很擅长逃出限制」，而 AMP 自己的客户也报告过本地脚本意外拿到生产控制台访问权限的情况。他亲测过这套限权机制：坐 12 小时越洋航班、飞机 wifi 不稳定的情况下，让 agent 自主执行一次从单工作区到多工作区的数据库结构迁移，每上线一个阶段就自动盯着日志和数据库指标，出问题就自动回滚，全程只需要偶尔查看。

团队几乎不再用 GitHub 的 issue 和 PR 功能，主仓库还挂在 GitHub 上，只是因为迁移到自建代码托管（内部代号 Forge）还没完成，Quinn 说「这类东西不是突然死的，是慢慢没气儿了」。他对 CI 的必要性也提出了怀疑，理由是 agent 自己会在统一的沙盒环境里跑测试，但也承认自己「还没被完全说服」，大概「三周内」想法可能会变。团队 20 人不请产品经理和市场人员，内部把 agent 做的营销、社区监测这类工作称为「jellyware」（比软件更松散的自制工具），Quinn 说他用 Codex 当自己的「CMO」跑广告投放和 SEO 建议已经两个月，「效果和请一个真人顾问差不多」。他还提到 Google 的 Jeff Dean 离职后想尝试「五个人一间屋子能做出什么」，呼应了 AMP 自己的小团队理念。
items.summary_en:
Quinn Slack is the founder and CEO of Sourcegraph. He split the company in two: code search stayed under Sourcegraph (customers include nine of the top ten global tech companies by market cap and four of the six largest banks), while a 20-person team spun out to build the coding agent product AMP, a precedent he compares to David Sacks spinning Yammer out of Geni around 2009. The AMP team is a third Europe, a third US, a third Australia, and its newest feature, called "orbs," runs agents in a cloud sandbox you can walk away from, laptop closed, running many in parallel. Quinn says the team has used orbs more in the last three or four weeks than every workflow change from all of last year combined.

Quinn states plainly: "mandatory code review before it gets to main is dead, it's been dead since we started working on AMP." What replaces it is stronger individual ownership and accountability, paired with a "mean time to recovery over mean time to failure" operating philosophy, fix it within 15 minutes rather than trying to catch every problem in review beforehand. He admits this doesn't fit every kind of software, but for their fast-moving, end-user product, he argues it produces higher quality than waiting days for review would.

Quinn offers a specific counter to the dominant "agents are unsafe" narrative: giving a cloud agent an OIDC-issued, 30-minute read-only token to touch production logs or a database sounds scary, but it's actually safer than the status quo, an agent running unrestricted on a developer's laptop with access to every credential already authorized on that machine. He cites the Hugging Face incident, noting "agents are very good at escaping containment," and says AMP's own customers have reported local scripts accidentally reaching a production console. He tested the scoped-access approach himself: on a 12-hour transatlantic flight with spotty wifi, he had an agent autonomously run a multi-stage database migration (moving AMP from single-workspace to multi-workspace), monitoring logs and database metrics after each stage and rolling back automatically if anything looked wrong, needing only occasional check-ins.

The team barely touches GitHub's issues or PRs anymore, the main repo is still hosted there only because the migration to their own code hosting (internally called Forge) isn't finished, in Quinn's words, "these things don't die with a bang, they die with a whimper." He's also questioning whether CI is still necessary, since the agent already runs tests in a shared reproducible sandbox, though he admits he's "not fully convinced yet" and expects his mind might change "in three weeks." The 20-person team has no product manager or marketer, calling the agent-driven marketing and community-monitoring work they do instead "jellyware," looser than proper software. Quinn says he's used Codex as his "CMO" running ad spend and SEO advice for two months, "with roughly the same results" as hiring a human consultant. He also brings up Jeff Dean's departure from Google to try what a five-person room can build, echoing AMP's own small-team philosophy.
items.why: 这条与头条 Grok Bot 呼应，但角度相反：头条讲如何把 agent 产品交给外部用户，这条讲一家 agent 公司自己用 agent 重写了内部流程，并提出一个反直觉的论证——限权云端 agent 比不受限的本地 agent 更安全。对纠结于是否收紧 agent 权限的人，这条值得对照。
items.why_en: This item mirrors the banner story from the opposite direction: the banner is about building an agent product for others, this one is about an agent company having its own internal process rewritten by agents, and it makes a specific, counterintuitive argument, that a scoped cloud agent is safer than an unrestricted local one, worth checking against for anyone debating whether to tighten their own agent's permissions.

items.title: Latent Space测了161个品类，看AI推荐谁
items.title_en: Latent Space Tested 161 Categories to See Who AI Recommends
items.author: swyx & Alessio · Latent Space
items.summary:
Latent Space 推出一个“前沿 AEO 追踪器”（AEO，Answer Engine Optimization，答案引擎优化）：用 6 种问法测试 7 个前沿模型，在 161 个品类里问“该选哪个产品或服务”，覆盖 coding agent、AI 播客、AI sandbox，以及管理数据库、天使投资人、企业报销软件等冷门品类。每条回答由 GPT-6 Astra 抽提并打分，计分标准为首选、备选、被提及分别加权，模型主动劝退某选项则扣分。

结果可见明显的自家偏好：Fable/Opus（Claude 系列）推荐 Claude Code，Sol/Astra（OpenAI 系列）推荐 Codex，Grok 推荐 Cursor，Muse 推荐自家 Muse Code，SWE-1.7 推荐 Devin。但也有反例——文章特别指出 GPT 系模型也会推荐 Claude，称这是“值得表扬的不偏心”。161 个品类中，28 个所有模型一致推荐同一产品，没有悬念；其余多为几家产品贴身竞争的“AEO 主战场”。

具体数据发现：Anthropic 新模型 Fable 比上一代 Opus 明显查更多来源才给出答案（中位数 15 个对 11 个），而 OpenAI 新模型 Astra 比上一代 Sol 查得更少，也更“自信”（中位数 5 个对 9 个），换问法几乎不改答案。作者认为，查证越少、越自信，AEO 对该厂商模型的用户就越有价值，因为答案随机性低，更易被针对性优化。文章还验证了此前 Ora 和 Vercel 的说法：网站做“markdown 内容协商”可提高被模型引用的概率，不做则会被模型直接跳过。

作者承认，目前测试未能纳入 Gemini/Antigravity、GLM/Zcode、DeepSeek/DeepCode，因报错与限流导致这几家难以稳定跑完，团队公开征集这几家厂商帮助提高限额。
items.summary_en:
Latent Space built a "Frontier AEO Tracker" (AEO: Answer Engine Optimization), running 6 prompt variations against 7 frontier models across 161 categories asking which product or service to pick, everything from coding agents, AI podcasts, and AI sandboxes to niche categories like managed databases, angel investors, and expense software. Each answer was extracted and scored by GPT-6 Astra, weighting first choices, alternative mentions, and plain mentions, with negative weight for any model actively warning against an option.

The results show obvious self-preference: Fable/Opus (Claude) recommends Claude Code, Sol/Astra (OpenAI) recommends Codex, Grok recommends Cursor, Muse recommends its own Muse Code, SWE-1.7 recommends Devin. But there are counterexamples too, the piece specifically calls out GPT models recommending Claude, calling it "a laudable nonbias." Of the 161 categories, 28 have every model universally agreeing on the same top pick, no contest there; most of the rest are tight, multi-way contests, the real battlegrounds for AEO.

One concrete finding: Anthropic's new model, Fable, checks noticeably more sources before answering than its predecessor Opus (median 15 vs. 11), while OpenAI's new model, Astra, checks fewer and is more "confident" than its predecessor Sol (median 5 vs. 9), barely changing its answer even if you lightly rephrase the question. The authors argue that the less a model verifies and the more confident it is, the more valuable AEO becomes for that model's audience, less randomness in the answer means more room for targeted optimization to actually move it. The piece also validated a claim Ora and Vercel had made earlier: sites that do "markdown content negotiation" really do get cited more, sites that don't get skipped over entirely.

The authors admit they couldn't reliably include Gemini/Antigravity, GLM/Zcode, or DeepSeek/DeepCode this round, errors and rate limits made them untenable, and they're publicly asking those companies for help raising the limits.
items.why: 首次有人将“AI 替用户挑选产品”这一现象量化为可查、可复现的排行榜，而非道听途说。对任何做内容或产品、关心自己是否会被 AI 推荐的人，这可直接对照自身品类，详见今日上手。
items.why_en: This is the first time someone has turned "which product AI recommends" into a queryable, reproducible ranking instead of anecdote. For anyone building content or a product who cares whether AI recommends them, this is a tool you can check your own category against directly, see tonight's hands-on.

items.title: OpenAI抢发百万美元数学题解，原研究者在Anthropic工作
items.title_en: OpenAI Races to Publish a Million-Dollar Math Proof, the Original Researcher Works at Anthropic
items.author: Simon Willison
items.summary:
OpenAI 用未发布内部模型，给出纳维-斯托克斯存在性与光滑性问题的解——这是七个“千禧年大奖难题”之一，2000 年 5 月 24 日悬赏 100 万美元，至今仅庞加莱猜想被解开。结果一出，即被“抢发”争议盖过：NYU 数学教授 Tristan Buckmaster 与在 Anthropic 工作的数学家 Levent Alpöge，花近一年时间借助 Claude 和 Codex（主要是 GPT-5.6 Sol）研究相关问题，8 月 15 日取得突破。传言传至 OpenAI，OpenAI 主动联系二人，才发现对方也在攻关同一方向。

Tristan 公开写下了交涉过程：他询问 OpenAI 团队第一条相关提示词何时发出，对方起初未正面回答，后承认是“过去几天内”，即听说他们工作之后才启动；他又追问模型是否看过或训练过他们存放在 Codex 中的全部草稿，回复是“模型不查用户数据”，但追问训练是否用及，对方未正面回答。OpenAI 提出可等 Tristan 发表，或让他做联名作者，但明确表示 Levent 不能挂名，理由是 Levent 的雇主 Anthropic 与 OpenAI 存在竞争关系。

OpenAI 的说法是：9 月 1 日听闻两个千禧年难题被解开的传言后，启动项目，用内部模型跑遍所有未解决的千禧年难题及其他高价值问题；9 月 5 日，首批 agent 启动 88 小时后，agent 组给出纳维-斯托克斯问题之解，又花 17 小时用 GPT-6 Astra 完成 Lean 形式化验证。解此题，agent 发了 270 万条消息，耗约 1300 亿输出 token（按 GPT-6 Astra 公开 API 价换算，解决全部问题总耗 3000 亿输出 token，价值约 1500 万美元）。OpenAI 称未以任何方式接触对方的发表前工作，“虽然不太可能，但不能排除通过我们产品使用数据脱敏后间接改进模型”。

Simon Willison 将此事类比网络安全圈现状：“只要听说漏洞传言，就足以让人用 agent 抢先挖出”，数学界亦然——得知某难题有未发表解，即可能触发数百万美元算力抢跑。他提出假设性问题：若他用 ChatGPT 头脑风暴未来公司方向，该想法会否经由训练影响后续模型，令他人抢先实现。菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩同日发声，称好的、有生产力的数学开放问题正被“不可再生地”挖掘，趋于稀缺，“即使只是听说有人在做某题的传言，也足以引发大规模 AI 算力去抢在原研究团队充分发挥之前将其铲平”，这可能使研究者不再愿意公开分享有前景的方向，逆转科学界数百年公开共享的传统。
items.summary_en:
OpenAI used an unreleased internal model to produce a resolution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems carrying a $1 million bounty since May 24, 2000, of which only the Poincaré conjecture has ever been solved. The result was immediately overshadowed by accusations of scooping: NYU math professor Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge, a mathematician who works at Anthropic, had spent nearly a year working on related problems using Claude and Codex (mainly GPT-5.6 Sol), reaching a breakthrough on August 15. Word spread through the math rumor mill to OpenAI, who reached out to the pair and discovered they were working the same problem.

Tristan published an account of what followed: he asked when OpenAI's first related prompt had been sent, and got no direct answer at first, eventually learning it was "in the past few days," meaning after OpenAI had already heard about his and Levent's work. He then asked whether the model had seen or been trained on the full drafts of their project, stored in Codex the whole time, and was told the model "did not look up user data," but got no answer when he pressed on whether it had been used in training. OpenAI offered to wait for Tristan to publish, or to make him a co-author on their own paper, but was clear Levent could not be a co-author, because his employer, Anthropic, competes with OpenAI.

OpenAI's own account: on September 1, hearing rumors that two Millennium Prize problems had been resolved, it launched an effort to test its internal model against every unsolved Millennium Prize problem and other high-value open problems. By September 5, about 88 hours after the first agents launched, the agents arrived at a resolution to Navier-Stokes, with an additional 17 hours of Lean formalization and verification via GPT-6 Astra. Solving Navier-Stokes alone took 2.7 million agent messages and roughly 130 billion output tokens (across every problem attempted, 300 billion output tokens, worth about $15 million at GPT-6 Astra's public API pricing). OpenAI says it never accessed the pair's pre-publication work through any means, "while unlikely, we cannot rule out that de-identified data derived from their usage of our products helped improve our models."

Simon Willison draws a parallel to computer security: "just a rumor of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days," and argues the same is now true of mathematics, just knowing an unpublished solution exists to a problem can trigger millions of dollars of LLM spending to get there first. He poses a new hypothetical: if he brainstorms a future company idea with ChatGPT, could that idea influence training in a way that helps a competitor beat him to it later. Fields Medalist Terence Tao spoke up the same day, warning that good, productive open math problems are being mined in a "non-renewable" way and becoming scarce, "even the rumor of someone working on a problem can trigger a massive amount of AI-powered effort to flatten it before the original research project has time to reach its full potential," which could push researchers to stop sharing promising directions altogether, reversing centuries of open science tradition.
items.why: 这一条呼应了过去几天反复出现的 agent 安全叙事，但切入角度不同，并非安全事故，而是学术信誉与署名权被同一种“传言触发抢跑”机制冲击，且已波及此前被认为远离商业竞争的纯数学领域。
items.why_en: This item echoes the agent-safety narrative that's run through the last several days, but from a completely different angle, not a security incident, but academic credit and authorship attribution hit by the exact same "rumor triggers a race" mechanism, this time reaching into pure mathematics, a field that seemed furthest from commercial competition.
